title: An affine punctured Noetherian local spectrum has dimension at most one
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ (so $A$ is local). Let $P=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ be the open subscheme of its prime spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion]. If $P$ is affine [def-pc-scheme], then $\dim A\leq1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Tag 0BCR, lemma-affine-punctured-spec, the only-if implication; statement at lines 3349–3352 and proof at lines 3355–3406.

proof.text: Put $N=\sqrt{(0)}$. Every prime contains $N$, so the quotient-spectrum identification gives an inclusion-preserving bijection between the prime ideals of $A$ and $A/N$. Thus their dimensions agree. The ring $A/N$ is local and Noetherian: its ideals lift to ideals of $A$ and the images of finite generating sets generate them. The quotient closed immersion restricted to the affine open $P$ has affine inverse image by the closed-immersion affine-cover criterion; this inverse image is the punctured spectrum of $A/N$. It suffices therefore to prove the assertion for reduced $A$. If $\dim A=0$ we are done; assume $\dim A\geq1$.

The minimal primes of $A$ are finite in number. None is $\mathfrak m$: if $\mathfrak m$ were minimal, every prime, being contained in the unique maximal ideal, would equal $\mathfrak m$, contrary to $\dim A\geq1$. Prime avoidance therefore gives $f\in\mathfrak m$ outside every minimal prime. Since $A$ is reduced, the zerodivisor criterion says multiplication by $f$ on $A$ is injective.

Write $P=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and let $\rho:A\to B$ be restriction. For every $g\in\mathfrak m$, $D_A(g)\subseteq P$. Pullback of basic opens identifies it with $D_B(\rho(g))$; basic-open sections of the structure sheaf identify their rings as $A_g$ and $B_{\rho(g)}$, compatibly with restriction. Hence $A_g\to B_{\rho(g)}$ is an isomorphism. In particular this holds for $g=f$. Since $A\to A_f$ is injective and factors through $B$, $\rho$ is injective. Multiplication by $f$ is also injective on $B$: at each point of $P$ its stalk is a localization of multiplication by $f$ on $A$, hence injective; a section with all germs zero is zero.

View $A\subseteq B$ and set $Q=B/A$. Localizing this quotient is exact. The isomorphisms of the preceding step give $Q_g=0$ for $g\in\mathfrak m$, in particular $Q_f=0$, so every element of $Q$ is killed by a power of $f$. If $\mathfrak p\ne\mathfrak m$, choose $g\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak p$; every element of $Q$ is killed by some power of $g$, so its image in $Q_{\mathfrak p}$ is zero. Thus $Q_{\mathfrak p}=0$. The same holds for its submodule $Q[f]$ by localization exactness.

There is an exact sequence $0\to Q[f]\xrightarrow{\delta}A/fA\to B/fB\to Q/fQ\to0$. Explicitly, for $q=b+A$ with $fq=0$, set $\delta(q)=fb+fA$; changing $b$ by an element of $A$ does not change this class. If $fb\in fA$, injectivity of multiplication by $f$ on $B$ gives $b\in A$, so $\delta$ is injective. Its image is the kernel of $A/fA\to B/fB$: if $a=fb$ in $B$, use $q=b+A$. Finally $b+fB\mapsto(b+A)+fQ$ is surjective, and its kernel is the image of $A/fA$, by subtracting $fc$ from a representative whenever $b+A=f(c+A)$. As a submodule of the finite module $A/fA$, $Q[f]$ is finite. If it is nonzero, its support is contained in $\{\mathfrak m\}$ by the preceding step, so the finite-support length lemma applies; if it is zero its length is zero. In both cases $Q[f]$ has finite length.

Apply the power-torsion cokernel bound to $Q$ and $f$: every element is killed by a power of $f$, and $Q[f]$ has finite length. Therefore $Q/fQ$ has finite length. A finite simple filtration shows it is finitely generated: simple factors are cyclic (any nonzero element generates), and lifting their generators successively generates the extension. The exact sequence in the preceding step now shows $B/fB$ is finite over $A/fA$: its image from $A/fA$ is cyclic, and lifts of a finite set of generators of $Q/fQ$, together with $1$, generate $B/fB$.

The spectrum of the finite ring map $A/fA\to B/fB$ is a finite morphism and hence a closed map. Its image is exactly $V_A(f)\cap P$: indeed $\operatorname{Spec}(B/fB)$ identifies with the zero locus of $\rho(f)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B=P$, and the quotient-spectrum identifications give precisely this subset of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/fA)$. Thus the punctured spectrum of $A/fA$ is closed. It must be empty: any nonempty closed subset of the spectrum of a local ring contains its closed point, since a prime in that subset is contained in the maximal ideal. Consequently $A/fA$ has exactly one prime ideal, its maximal ideal (it is nonzero since $f\in\mathfrak m$), and $\dim(A/fA)=0$.

Apply dimension drop for the nonzerodivisor $f\in\mathfrak m$ in the Noetherian local ring $A$: $\dim A=\dim(A/fA)+1=1$. Together with the dimension-zero case and the equality of dimensions before and after reduction, this proves $\dim A\leq1$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-O1-0cf368177 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 0BCR (divisors.tex 3349-3406). The item states the only-if direction (Noetherian local A, affine punctured spectrum implies dim A <= 1) with the same hypotheses and conclusion. All 8 steps follow the source's proof and every non-elementary fact cites a node whose statement says it. (1) Reduction to A/N: 00E5 gives an inclusion-preserving bijection of primes, 01IG gives the closed immersion, and clause (1) of 01QO makes the inverse image of P (the punctured spectrum of A/N) affine. (2) 00FR, then prime avoidance 00DS, then 00EW(3) give a nonzerodivisor f in m. (3) Basic-open pullback plus tilde sections give A_g = B_{rho g} for g in m. rho is injective through A to A_f. f is injective on B through germs, using 01HV(c) localization and 00CS exactness. (4) is elementary and correct: Q_g = 0, Q is f-power torsion, and Q[f] is supported in {m}; containment is stated rather than the source's equality, which is right when Q[f] = 0. (5) I checked the exact sequence 0 -> Q[f] -> A/fA -> B/fB -> Q/fQ -> 0 by representatives. Q[f] is finite by 00IK and has finite length by 00L5, with the zero case handled separately. (6) The new node bounds length(Q/fQ); the simple filtration makes Q/fQ finitely generated, so A/fA -> B/fB is finite. (7) 01WI and 01WN make Spec(B/fB) -> Spec(A/fA) a closed map; its image is the punctured spectrum of A/fA, which must therefore be empty, so dim A/fA = 0. (8) 00KW gives dim A = 1. The new node lem-sfb-power-torsion-cokernel-length (R commutative, Q f-power torsion, length Q[f] = l finite, then length(Q/fQ) <= l) is true by the K_n = Q[f^n] argument. I tested it on Q = 0, f = 0, f a unit, a DVR with K/R and with R/f^n, and an infinite direct sum, where the hypothesis fails. It is self-contained, statement-only, not a clause of the item, and has no duplicate in the DAG (grepped 0BCR, Q[f], power torsion, length with torsion); its three kinds of search are recorded.
